recent_posts.title: How Wix migrated 1000 MySQL servers to Graviton in 30 days with zero downtime
recent_posts.summary: Wix's DB Infrastructure team migrated over 1,000 MySQL servers across 160+ clusters from Intel-based EC2 instances to AWS Graviton CPUs in just one month — three times faster than the planned timeline — with zero downtime. The migration also involved moving from EOL CentOS 7 to Amazon Linux 2023. The team automated the entire process using AWX (Ansible) and Wix's Internal Developer Platform, breaking the workflow into modular building blocks that emulated DBA manual steps. A 'no rollback' policy backed by automated health checks kept momentum high. Results included a ~15% reduction in MySQL compute costs, up to ~50% reduction in CPU utilization, 500 fewer total cores used, and significant reductions in IOPS and disk throughput. Key lessons: avoid over-engineering the design phase, look for optimization opportunities within migration projects, and leverage cross-team collaboration between DBAs, DevOps, and developers.

recent_posts.title: The xEngineer: A New Blueprint for Software Engineering in the AI Era
recent_posts.summary: Wix Engineering introduces the 'xEngineer' concept, arguing that AI tools like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor are shifting the software engineer's role from code writer to problem definer, system designer, and AI orchestrator. Three key principles define this shift: using AI across the entire engineering lifecycle (not just code generation), enabling smaller teams with end-to-end ownership by reducing cross-domain friction, and building products around probabilistic LLM-driven systems. The post draws on a public discussion with Wix's CTO and VP Engineering, who argue that deep expertise still matters but the baseline expectation is changing toward full-stack capability augmented by AI. The core message is that engineering value now lies in judgment, architecture, and orchestration rather than syntax mastery.

recent_posts.title: Beyond Enthusiasm: A 5-Week, 86-Developer AI Coding Experiment
recent_posts.summary: Wix Engineering ran a structured 5-week experiment with 86 developers across four countries to measure the real productivity impact of Claude Code versus Cursor and an internal tool called Astra. GitHub data (commits, PRs, lines changed) was analyzed using a Difference-in-Differences approach against 90-day baselines. Key findings: Cursor showed almost no measurable productivity lift despite users reporting feeling more productive; Claude Code showed significant output gains, but only after developers built trust and stopped micromanaging it. 47% of exit survey respondents said they accomplished tasks they wouldn't have attempted before. The experiment is now driving a company-wide rollout, but the author warns of an emerging 'AI Curse'—individual productivity exploding while organizational coordination, CI/CD pipelines, and review processes become the new bottleneck.

recent_posts.title: Data-to-Production: Bridging the Gap Between Iceberg and Live Microservices
recent_posts.summary: Wix built a Data-to-Production platform that bridges their petabyte-scale Iceberg data warehouse with production microservices requiring millisecond latency. The system consists of three layers: a self-service metadata registration console with human-in-the-loop governance, a dynamic Airflow-based ingestion engine supporting three loading strategies (OVERWRITE, UPSERT, PARTITION_REPLACE) with custom idempotent operators, and a type-safe Scala serving layer using a semantic JSON DSL that compiles to optimized ClickHouse SQL. The platform handles billions of rows, automatic schema evolution, catch-up logic, and includes safety mechanisms like empty staging protection and row count validation, while preventing SQL injection and enforcing resource governance.

recent_posts.title: Building an AI agent that automates Airflow incident investigation and saves 675 engineering hours monthly
recent_posts.summary: Wix built AirBot, an AI-powered Slack agent that automates incident investigation for their 3,500+ Apache Airflow pipelines. The system uses LLMs with Model Context Protocol to analyze logs, identify root causes, and generate pull requests automatically. By leveraging Socket Mode for security, LangChain for reasoning, and tiered model selection (GPT-4o Mini for classification, Claude 4.5 Opus for complex analysis), AirBot saves 675 engineering hours monthly. The architecture includes custom MCP integrations with GitHub, Trino, Spark, and OpenMetadata, achieving a 15% fully automated fix rate and 66% positive feedback across 60 engineers.

recent_posts.title: From Syntax Checker to Critical Reviewer: How We Convinced AI to Catch Real API Quality Issues
recent_posts.summary: AI naturally gravitates toward catching easy technical issues like formatting and naming patterns while missing critical developer experience problems in API design. By restructuring prompts to heavily weight developer usability, adding explicit verification checklists, and linking technical guidelines to developer impact, the team forced their AI tool to catch real quality issues like hidden cognitive complexity, misleading field names, and workflow friction. The key insight: AI needs structured constraints to prioritize quality over technical correctness, which becomes increasingly important as AI takes on more API design tasks.

recent_posts.title: Why I Stop Prompting and Start Logging: The Design-Log Methodology
recent_posts.summary: The Design-Log Methodology addresses the "Context Wall" problem in AI-assisted coding by maintaining version-controlled markdown documents that capture design decisions before implementation. Instead of repeatedly explaining architecture to AI, developers create immutable design logs in a ./design-log/ folder that document problems, questions, answers, and implementation plans. The AI reads these logs first, asks clarifying questions in the document, and only codes after design approval. This approach transforms AI from a code generator into an architectural partner, enabling simple prompts, preventing context drift, and creating traceable implementation history.

recent_posts.title: The Wix Engineering 2025 Review: AI, Platforms, Data, and Deep Technical Lessons-Learned
recent_posts.summary: Wix Engineering shares a comprehensive year-in-review covering their journey building and operating at massive scale. Key themes include transitioning to AI-first development with production-ready LLM systems, platform engineering treating internal tools as products, cost optimization cutting data platform expenses by 50%, migrating to monorepo architecture for 30M+ lines of code, and reliability patterns for microservices. The review includes deep dives on Spark-as-a-Service running 5,000+ daily jobs, Kafka optimization reducing costs by 30%, RAG evaluation tools, context engineering for AI systems, and developer productivity improvements like 50× faster integration testing. Lessons span from technical implementation details to organizational transformation and engineering culture.

recent_posts.title: Platform engineering is a distinct discipline from DevOps
recent_posts.summary: Platform engineering is a distinct discipline from DevOps that treats internal infrastructure as a product, focusing on building reusable self-service systems that hide operational complexity. While DevOps accelerates delivery through collaboration and automation, platform engineering creates golden paths and abstractions that allow developers to ship business value without needing deep infrastructure expertise. At scale, mature platforms connect velocity, safety, cost, and business KPIs, transforming technical decisions into strategic business capabilities. Wix demonstrates this through their Safe Production Changes system, where load balancer configurations are managed as code with gradual rollouts, automated health checks, and business-aware monitoring.

recent_posts.title: How context engineering reduced AI costs by 23× and improved speed by 46%
recent_posts.summary: Context engineering, the practice of preprocessing and optimizing data before sending it to LLMs, can dramatically improve AI system performance. By implementing a structured pipeline that ranks candidates with utility functions, uses semantic slugs instead of opaque IDs, optimizes token usage, and minimizes LLM output, Wix reduced costs by 23× and improved response times by 46%. This approach enabled switching from expensive models to Gemini Flash 2.0, proving that data preparation matters more than prompt tuning for building efficient AI agents.
